rationale: Thirty-fifth pass: put the persistence accounting under execution. The recorded behavior says a conflicting append lowers the saved index so the replaced entries are reported again as unsaved; a violation would let a truncated entry be treated as already durable. The harness appends four entries to an entryLog over the package test log, acknowledges all four as saved, then appends a conflicting term at index 3 and emits the entries-to-save range before and after together with the resulting last index and term. That range is the exact quantity a lost-save defect would corrupt.

investigations.question: After a conflicting append replaces entries already acknowledged as saved, does the entry log report the replaced indexes again as unsaved, or can a truncated entry remain classified as durable?
investigations.hypothesis: The conflicting append lowers the saved index to the last index before the conflict, so entriesToSave begins at the first replaced index instead of returning empty.
investigations.discriminator: The before and after first index and length of entriesToSave, and the resulting last index and term.

scope.description: Observe entriesToSave before and after a conflicting append over entries acknowledged as saved.

experiment.prefix: An entryLog is created over the package in-memory test log. Four entries with term 1 at indexes 1 to 4 are appended and an UpdateCommit with StableLogTo 4 and StableLogTerm 1 acknowledges them as saved. tryAppend is then called with LogIndex 2 and two entries at indexes 3 and 4 with term 2, which conflict with the saved entries. entriesToSave is read before and after, and the last index and term are reported. No raft node, transport or storage engine participates.
